mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover from their recent lows, commuter exposure to retail corridors rises and RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks. The signal should be positive if the rebound persists for at least two consecutive weekly observations.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, reject this mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RESIDENTIAL time below its recent elevated range releases time from home into out-of-home consumption, pushing RETAIL_REC up within one to two weeks. The effect is strongest after residential mobility falls back from its local peak.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6.5 after being above 8.0 in the prior two weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below the stated threshold but RETAIL_REC does not rise within the next 14 days relative to the prior 14 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after an unusually weak spell signals reopening leisure activity and broader weekend movement, which then spills into retail visits. RETAIL_REC should improve over the next four weeks when PARKS rises from deeply negative levels.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week after being below -30
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds by at least 15 points from below -30 and RETAIL_REC still does not exceed its prior 4-week average over the following month, reject this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply depressed together, the city is still operating under mobility restraint conditions and discretionary shopping demand stays weak. In that regime, RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -40 and -15 respectively but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Higher GROCERY_PHARM mobility alongside stable RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates substitution toward essential trips rather than discretionary outings, which suppresses retail-and-recreation demand over the next one to two weeks. The effect should appear quickly if grocery trips absorb household errand time.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 and RETAIL_REC nevertheless increases within 14 days, reject this mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent recovery in TRANSIT combined with improving WORKPLACES reflects renewed daily circulation into city centers, which supports retail foot traffic with a lag of about four weeks. RETAIL_REC should trend upward if both series continue to climb from current depressed levels.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior 4-week average, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: After an abrupt rebound in PARKS, outdoor leisure draws spending away from enclosed retail for roughly one week before normal shopping resumes. This creates a short-run negative effect on RETAIL_REC when park visits jump from deeply negative readings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 20 points in a single week
failure_condition: If PARKS jumps by more than 20 points and RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 7 days, reject this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls from its elevated level while TRANSIT stays weak, it signals people are leaving home for non-work reasons rather than returning to commuting, which delays retail recovery. Under that mix, RETAIL_REC should remain flat to lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below 6 while TRANSIT stays below -40
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 6 while TRANSIT stays below -40 and RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the following 28 days, reject the hypothesis.
